question.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point $t>0$ on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨2t,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}⟨3t,\,2⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4})}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
